load.purpose: Working weight — the largest type in the product, read at arm's length.

readout.purpose: Weight / reps / RIR value inside a recessed field.

measure.purpose: All measurement data: weight, reps, RIR, dates, durations, units.

label.purpose: Field captions and chips, uppercase and tracked.

shadows.name: dome
shadows.purpose: Resting pressable surface — domes, secondary buttons, steppers, day cells. Low amplitude on purpose.

shadows.name: dome-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover, the live dome, and the suggested dome.

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.purpose: Recessed WHITE cavities — fields, wells, loading bars, empty states, disabled controls.

shadows.name: sunk
shadows.purpose: Recessed COLOURED cells — logged and missed domes, active nav item. The white half would read as haze on a saturated fill.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Containers and filled buttons sitting on the board — cards, panels, chart shell, timer shell.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: The nav film. Only ever used over the colour bloom, where the blur is visible.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The authored moment: convex to pressed. Every state transition inherits it.

motion.name: burst
motion.purpose: The foil ring opening once on a logged set, scale(.72) to scale(1.34), fading out.

motion.name: breathe
motion.purpose: The live dome's halo. One of only two loops allowed in the system.

motion.name: settling
motion.purpose: Loading bars pulsing 1 to 0.48 opacity. No sweeping shimmer.

narrative.overview:
A weekly compliance dose card: a white board, a clear film, and rows of cells you press one at a time. The card carries the plan, printed and permanent. Pressing a dome does not change the card, it changes one cell. A Placement is an unpressed dome, a Session is a pressed cell, and history is the card you can no longer un-press.

Three materials, each with one job. Solid white is the ground and the resting state of everything — flat fills, no gradients on surfaces. Light carves the depth: a restrained pair of soft shadows, cool below-right and white above-left, small enough to give a component a body without becoming the aesthetic. Saturated colour provides the contrast the white would otherwise lack — recorded and active cells are filled solid with their hue, not tinted with a pale wash. Glass appears rarely and only where it can actually be seen, floating over colour.

Light by decision, not by category: the scene is a gym floor at arm's length, one hand occupied, under bright fluorescents or window glare. A solid coloured cell is legible there; a pale wash is not.
keyCharacteristics: Solid white surfaces. No gradient fills on any component face.
Neumorphic depth at low amplitude — 4 px offsets, ~30% alpha — to give components a body.
Colour is the contrast device: state cells are filled solid, not washed.
Glass appears only over colour, where blur is visible and doing work.
Two depth states carry meaning: raised is pressable, sunk is recorded.
One authored motion moment — the press — that every other transition inherits.
Archivo's width axis does the work a second display face would; mono is measurement only.

rules.name: The Solid Surface Rule
rules.body: Component faces are flat solid fills. No gradient stands in for depth — if a surface needs to look raised, that is the shadow's job, not a two-stop ramp across its face.

rules.name: The Fill-Not-Wash Rule
rules.body: State is carried by a solid saturated fill with white (or, for amber, dark) text. Pale washes are decoration and they disappear in gym light.

rules.name: The One Concept Per Hue Rule
rules.body: A hue names a state and nothing else. Green is not 'success', it is actual. Red is not 'danger', it is missed or deviated.

rules.name: The Ink Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text token is verified against the composited surface it actually sits on. Filled cells always use the -ink variant, never the base hue, because white on the base hue fails at 3.5:1.

rules.name: The Measurement-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is for data — numbers, units, dates, identifiers. If it is a sentence, it is Archivo.

rules.name: The Width-Not-Weight Rule
rules.body: Emphasis at large sizes comes from the wdth axis, not from a second family or a colour. 118 for load and clock, 112 for display and headline, 100 everywhere else.

rules.name: The Low-Amplitude Rule
rules.body: Soft shadows stay at 4 px offset and ~30% alpha. If a component looks moulded out of putty, the shadow is doing the design's job instead of the colour's.

rules.name: The Coloured Cavity Rule
rules.body: pressed is for white; sunk is for colour. Never put the white half of the pair on a saturated fill — it reads as haze, not as depth.

rules.name: The Visible-Glass Rule
rules.body: Glass only goes where there is colour behind it. Frosted white over flat white is an invisible material and a wasted backdrop-filter.

rules.name: The Cool Light Rule
rules.body: Shadows are rgba(148,163,193,…), never black except the coloured-cavity inset, and never chromatic.

rules.name: The 48 Rule
rules.body: Every interactive control is at least 48 px tall. The single exemption is the 7-column calendar week grid at ~41 px.

dos: Do fill component faces with a flat solid colour and let the shadow carry the depth.
Do keep soft shadows at ~4 px offset and ~30% alpha — a body, not a moulding.
Do fill state cells solid with the -ink hue and white text (amber takes dark ink instead).
Do pick the hue from the concept, not the emotion: blue = Planned, green = Actual, violet = Progression, red = Missed, amber = Live.
Do use sunk on coloured cavities and pressed on white ones.
Do put glass only over the colour bloom, where the blur is visible.
Do make the active Set the largest object on screen and place it in the lower third.
Do keep every interactive control at or above 48 px, and give load numerals the wdth 118 axis.
Do verify text against the composited surface, translucency included.
Do show what was performed on a logged dome, never the target it was measured against.
Do name the problem and the recovery in every error string.
Do self-host every font as woff2 — the app makes no runtime network requests.
donts: Don't put a gradient on a component face. Depth is light, not a two-stop ramp.
Don't raise the shadow amplitude to make something feel tactile; that is 2010s neumorphism and it turns the whole UI into grey putty.
Don't signal state with a pale wash. Washes vanish in gym light; fills do not.
Don't put the white half of the shadow pair on a saturated fill — it reads as haze.
Don't use backdrop-filter where there is no colour behind it.
Don't push the canvas to pure #FFFFFF, and don't darken it into grey.
Don't re-enable a pressed cell. A record is not a control.
Don't introduce chamfers, cut corners, or hard block shadows — that is the discarded Cloud Quarry world.
Don't set prose in Martian Mono, or any measurement in Archivo.
Don't nest a card inside a card; use a recessed well.
Don't add a sixth hue, a second display face, or a dark theme.
Don't animate width, height, or padding; the rest-timer rail scales, it does not resize.
Don't loop an animation. The press fires once, and only the live dome and the loading state are allowed to repeat.
